tagline: AI · dev tools · tech — a two-minute read

lead.headline: OpenAI's chief scientist wants industry-wide limits on AI, measured in perplexity
lead.summary: In a Sunday essay, Jakub Pachocki argues that perplexity (how well a model predicts the next token) should become the shared yardstick for AI progress, and publishes OpenAI's own internal numbers for the first time. He proposes common limits that labs commit not to cross until monitoring of AI behaviour reaches a concrete milestone, such as a successor to chain-of-thought monitors, and warns that AI-driven pretraining breakthroughs could arrive as soon as 2027. Sam Altman called it the most important thing OpenAI has published in a while.

number_of_day.label: The log-perplexity at which, Pachocki says, OpenAI's model started producing groundbreaking maths results. GPT-3.5 sat at ~0.99, GPT-4 at ~0.91.

news.headline: Startup says AI agents designed a brand-new CPU architecture from scratch
news.summary: Palo Alto's Architect Labs says its AI systems discovered, designed and verified Frostbite, a general-purpose CPU with a new instruction set built around interaction nets. In simulation, a four-tile 7nm cluster delivered 4.59x the performance per watt of a dual-issue in-order core across 25 workloads (3.83x without AI tuning). It has not been made in silicon yet.

news.headline: Signal blocks screenshots on Android and iOS to keep OS-level AI agents out of chats
news.summary: Meredith Whittaker called agentic operating systems an "existential threat": once an OS agent scans the screen, the data is out of Signal's control. Screenshot blocking, already default on Windows, now comes to mobile. Users can switch it off, which she says breaks Signal's privacy guarantees, and she admits it is an incomplete fix.

news.headline: Altman backs the limits proposal; Reuters frames it against fast-growing risk concerns
news.summary: Pachocki wants a first industry-wide development limit plus defined milestones that must be met before passing it. Altman said on X that the industry should seek agreement on common limits. The post also concedes that publishing internal perplexity figures gives competitors a clearer view of where OpenAI stands.

x_posts.name: Jeremy Howard
x_posts.text: I think a lot of the folks in the "software is solved" camp aren't being bold enough. If you try to do something really really difficult, well beyond what anyone has previously achieved in the field, you'll see the limitations and opportunities clearly.
x_posts.why: A useful test for any coding agent: aim it at something nobody has done before.

x_posts.name: Ethan Mollick
x_posts.text: Yes, it is reasonable to expect AI models struggle more with unverifiable domains, but I do think it is worth noting that we also see very large gains in domains without automatic verification as well. Here are human evaluations of AI in writing, business problems, design, etc.
x_posts.why: Pushes back on the idea that AI only improves where answers can be checked automatically.

writers_corner.title: The Most Powerful Attitude You Can Take Toward Your Life and the Life of the World
writers_corner.take: Through Richard Powers' advice to the next generation, Popova argues that small deliberate acts still reshape the world, and that algorithmic search has quietly taken away the joy of stumbling onto things.
writers_corner.quote: Somewhere along the way of choices being made for us by an insular tribe of technologists, discovery was sacrificed at the altar of search
